title: Abdominal and pelvic MRI
what: A machine with a strong magnet takes detailed pictures of the organs in your belly and pelvis. There is no X-ray radiation.
why: To look more closely at changes in the liver, pancreas, kidneys, or pelvic organs, if an ultrasound or CT did not give a full answer.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes, longer with contrast
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, metal implants, metal fragments, clips, or an ear implant. This is important
If you are pregnant or might be pregnant
Kidney disease, if contrast is planned
If you are afraid of closed spaces
An IUD, or coil. Tell the staff in advance

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 4 to 6 hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: A light dinner without fizzy drinks, beans, raw vegetables, or dark rye bread. This means less gas in the bowel.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: For a pelvic scan, you are sometimes asked to come with a fairly full bladder. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Contrast
prepare.text: If contrast is planned, you are often asked for a recent creatinine blood test. It shows how your kidneys work.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Do not wear jewelry. Remove glitter makeup and anything metal on your clothes.

bring: Past ultrasound, CT, or MRI images and reports
Your creatinine test, if contrast is planned
Papers for your implant or pacemaker, if you have one
steps: You answer a form about metal and your health
You change and leave everything metal in a locker
If contrast is needed, an IV is put into a vein
Sometimes medicine is given so the bowel moves less
You lie on your back, and a flat coil is placed on your belly
The table slides into the scanner
You are often asked to breathe in and hold your breath for a few seconds
If contrast is needed, it is given in the middle of the scan
feel: The machine knocks loudly. You get earplugs or headphones
You need to lie still, which can be tiring
Contrast sometimes gives a cold feeling in your arm
You hold a call button. You can call the staff at any time
after: You can eat and drink right away, unless the doctor says otherwise
After contrast, drink more water that day
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
red_flags: After contrast: a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Why do I need to hold my breath during an abdominal MRI?
faq.a: Belly organs move when you breathe. When you hold your breath for a few seconds, the pictures come out sharp.

faq.q: Can I have an MRI with an IUD?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most IUDs are safe with MRI. But be sure to tell the staff in advance.
It is usually well tolerated. Your kidneys are checked before contrast, and you should mention any allergy in advance.

reminders.text: Abdominal MRI tomorrow. Have a light dinner, without fizzy drinks, beans, or raw vegetables.
From now on, you usually do not eat before the MRI. Check the time with your clinic. Do not wear jewelry.
